title: Charge sheet vs final report - what happens after police investigation
p1:
A police investigation ends… but does that always mean someone will face trial?

Many people think the police simply file a charge sheet after every investigation. The reality is more interesting.
p2: A charge sheet and a final report are not the same thing. A charge sheet means the police believe there is enough evidence to proceed against the accused. But a final report may also be filed when the investigation does not find sufficient evidence or when the case does not move forward for other reasons.
p3:
The surprising part: a police report is not the final decision on guilt or innocence. The court reviews the material and decides whether the case should proceed further.

So, a charge sheet does not mean someone is guilty, and a final report does not always mean the story ends there. The next step depends on the court’s view of the investigation and evidence.
conclusion: Before today, did you know that filing of a charge sheet only starts the court process and does not prove guilt? What was your understanding of it?
